themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints exploded to 5 reports THIS WEEK compared to a 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 3900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting either sudden infrastructure failure, removal, or overflow in a concentrated area worth immediate ground-truthing.
evidence: 5 litter basket complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3900% increase)
z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Spike is most recent and sharpest in entire dataset
reporting_angles: Are sanitation bins being removed or vandalized in specific neighborhoods? Check with Sanitation Department.
Talk to residents in affected blocks about whether this correlates with missed pickups or broken receptacles.

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 30 reports THIS WEEK versus a 12.1 weekly average—a 147% increase (z-score: 2.83)—concurrent with construction permit surge (587 filings in 90 days, 364 alterations), suggesting construction activity may be ramping up.
evidence: 30 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.1 weekly average (147% spike)
587 DOB building permits filed in past 90 days with 364 alterations active
z-score of 2.83 meets high-severity threshold for emerging issue
reporting_angles: Cross-reference noise complaints with DOB permit locations—are they clustered around active construction sites?
Interview residents near high-alteration zones about daytime/early-morning construction noise; check if permits are being violated.

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Disputes
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 6 reports LAST WEEK versus a 0.2 weekly baseline—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—potentially tied to seasonal reopenings or expansion of streetery programs that may lack proper management or community coordination.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (2300% increase)
No prior community board or news mentions suggest this is sudden, not anticipated
reporting_angles: Has the city expanded or reopened outdoor dining permits in Sheepshead Bay recently? Check with Department of Transportation.
Talk to nearby residents and business owners about what specifically triggered complaints—noise, obstruction, sanitation, or lack of notification.

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Tree Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 15 reports LAST WEEK versus a 4.2 weekly average—a 253% spike (z-score: 4.32)—indicating seasonal growth, deferred maintenance, or hazardous conditions that may threaten pedestrians and property.
evidence: 15 overgrown tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly baseline (253% increase)
z-score of 4.32 indicates sustained spike in high-severity range
Timing suggests seasonal spring growth coinciding with deferred Parks Department pruning
reporting_angles: Map 311 tree complaints against Parks Department maintenance schedules—are there deferred work orders?
Canvass complaints to identify if hazards involve downed branches, blocked sightlines at intersections, or property damage.

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Encampment Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Street obstructions and encampments show elevated but older spikes (3 weeks ago and earlier), with obstructions up 196% (z-score: 5.11) and encampments up 211% (z-score: 2.77), suggesting a multi-week deterioration in public space management, though neither is THIS WEEK's peak.
evidence: 30 obstruction complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 10.1 weekly baseline (196% spike, z-score 5.11)
7 encampment complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.2 weekly baseline (211% spike, z-score 2.77)
No recent community board or council constituent data to confirm sustained follow-up or resolution
reporting_angles: Are obstructions and encampments still present, or has the situation improved? Conduct field verification to assess current conditions.
Interview Parks, Sanitation, and NYPD about response protocols—why did both issues spike simultaneously 3 weeks ago?
